question: What is the primary purpose of follow-up care in mental health?

options.A: To provide ongoing support and monitoring after hospital discharge
options.B: To keep patients admitted in the psychiatric ward indefinitely
options.C: To replace the need for any formal medication or therapy
options.D: To punish patients who do not follow hospital rules

explanation: Follow-up care ensures that patients continue to receive support, check-ups, and monitoring after they leave the hospital setting. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is follow-up care considered essential for patients with chronic mental health conditions?

options.A: Patients no longer need family support once they leave the ward
options.B: Mental illnesses often require long-term monitoring to prevent symptom return
options.C: Community clinics have unlimited space for permanent admissions
options.D: Discharge medications are designed to cure the illness permanently

explanation: Because chronic mental health conditions fluctuate over time, ongoing care helps catch early changes before a full relapse occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of psychiatric follow-up care?

options.A: Isolating the patient from their family and community
options.B: Focusing solely on physical injuries rather than mood
options.C: Preventing relapse and maintaining symptom stability
options.D: Encouraging the patient to stop taking all medications

explanation: Keeping symptoms stable and preventing a return of acute illness is a central objective of ongoing mental health visits. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does setting small, realistic goals during follow-up visits help the patient?

options.A: It ensures the nurse does not have to do any paperwork
options.B: It replaces the need for any professional medical treatment
options.C: It builds their confidence and encourages active participation in recovery
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will never feel stressed again

explanation: Achievable goals empower patients, making them feel capable and involved in managing their own health. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is a key responsibility of the psychiatric nurse in continuing care?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff payroll budgets
options.B: Observing mental status and evaluating medication side effects
options.C: Prescribing brand new antipsychotic drugs independently
options.D: Diagnosing rare surgical disorders in the community

explanation: Nurses closely monitor how the patient is doing mentally and check for any troublesome reactions to prescribed drugs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is building a trusting relationship important during continuing care?

options.A: It legally binds the patient to live at the clinic
options.B: It keeps the patient engaged and compliant with their treatment plan
options.C: it stops family members from getting involved in care
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid documenting patient interactions

explanation: Trust makes patients feel safe sharing their true feelings and concerns, which helps prevent them from dropping out of care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: During a follow-up assessment, what must a nurse always screen for directly?

options.A: Thoughts of self-harm or harming others
options.D: The exact brand of soap the patient uses

explanation: Safety assessment, including checking for suicidal or aggressive thoughts, is a mandatory part of every mental health evaluation. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: A patient who previously appeared neat and well-groomed arrives at a follow-up visit looking disheveled with disorganized speech. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A potential worsening of mental status or failing condition
options.B: That the physical assessment is completely unnecessary
options.C: That the patient has changed career paths successfully
options.D: Normal improvement in daily living skills

explanation: Negative changes in personal hygiene and disorganized speech often signal that a patient is relapsing or struggling. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is a common reason why patients stop taking their psychiatric medications?

options.A: Medications always taste like sweet candy
options.B: The local pharmacy gives them too many refills
options.C: Because nurses tell them to stop after one week
options.D: Unpleasant side effects or feeling better and thinking they are cured

explanation: Patients often quit medications when side effects bother them or when they feel healthy and mistakenly believe they no longer need treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why should a nurse advise a patient never to stop psychiatric medication abruptly?

options.A: The patient will instantly lose all their memories
options.B: It is against hospital administrative policy to miss one dose
options.C: Doctors will refuse to see the patient ever again
options.D: Sudden discontinuation can trigger severe withdrawal or quick relapse

explanation: Abruptly stopping psychotropic drugs often causes a sudden return of acute symptoms or dangerous physical withdrawal effects. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h5)

question: What are early warning signs of a psychiatric relapse?

options.A: Immediate physical healing of a broken bone
options.B: Winning an award at work or school
options.D: Subtle changes like trouble sleeping, irritability, and withdrawing from others

explanation: Early warning signs are small behavioral or emotional shifts that appear before a major crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is it important to teach family members how to spot early warning signs?

options.A: Family members are qualified to prescribe psychiatric drugs
options.B: It removes all responsibility from the healthcare team
options.C: It ensures the family pays for all clinic supplies
options.D: Family members live with the patient and can spot changes early

explanation: Because relatives spend the most time with the patient at home, they are often the first to notice when behavior starts changing. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which professionals typically make up the multidisciplinary mental health team?

options.C: Nurses, psychiatrists, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Pharmacists and hospital security guards only

explanation: A comprehensive mental health team includes various specialists working together to address different recovery needs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why is connecting a patient to community resources like vocational training important?

options.A: It forces them to work without getting any rest
options.B: It ensures the clinic makes a financial profit
options.C: It replaces the need for talking to a nurse or doctor
options.D: It helps them regain independence and purpose through meaningful activity

explanation: Community resources like job training help patients reintegrate into society and build a fulfilling life after illness. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to psychiatric follow-up care in Nigeria?

options.A: Zero cultural stigma surrounding mental illness
options.B: Free transportation provided to all patients
options.C: Long distances to health facilities and high medication costs
options.D: An excess of psychiatric hospitals in every village

explanation: Financial strain and distance are major hurdles that prevent patients from attending regular clinic visits in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h8)

question: How should psychiatric nurses handle the reality that many patients visit traditional or spiritual healers?

options.A: Scold and punish patients for seeking help outside the hospital
options.B: Use cultural sensitivity and educate communities while respecting patients
options.C: Refuse treatment to anyone who has visited a healer
options.D: Ignore traditional beliefs and pretend they do not exist

explanation: Respectful dialogue and community education work much better than judgment in encouraging patients to accept orthodox mental healthcare. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h8)
